Mirrors DevKitC-1 J1. Pins 1-2 (3V3) and 21 (5V) are both INPUTS to the shield. Analog on 4-7 and 12, CAN on 9-11, SD bus on 15-20 -- grouped so each block routes away from the row rather than across it. Pin 3 is RST, pins 13/14 are IO3/IO46, all left open.

Mirrors DevKitC-1 J3. Pin 10 (IO38) is left open because it drives the dev board's RGB LED on v1.1; check the revision, some put it on IO48, which is the WS2812 output here.

Two 5V excitation pins, two Kelvin sense-ground pins, two current-carrying grounds, four signals. SENS_RTN must land on the SENSOR's ground stud, not on the same stud as pins 9/10
The second ADC's unused pair, brought out raw -- 0-3.3V only, no divider and no clamp in front of them. For a bench sensor, not for the loom

Ships OPEN: unterminated. Bridge the pads only when this board is an END node on its own bus. A vehicle's bus -- OBD-II diagnostics included -- is already terminated at both ends, and a third 120 ohm across the pair takes it to about 40 ohm and can stop it working. Defaulting terminated made that an easy mistake to make
Close for a raw 0-3.3V sensor (shorts the upper leg)

Ships BRIDGED 1-2 = the 0-5V range, which is what almost every automotive sensor is. Cut 1-2 and bridge 2-3 for 0-16V; cut 1-2 and leave both open for no divider (then close BYPASS3 for a raw 0-3.3V sensor). Defaulting to 0-5V also means the firmware's DIVIDER_GAIN matches the board as shipped. NOTE: moving a channel off the default breaks the match with the return attenuator, so that channel loses its ground rejection -- read it single-ended if you do

Inrush limit. 1206 for the pulse rating: 210 mA into 22 ohm is 1 W for the first instant, decaying with a 11 s time constant

Series limit. ISO 9141-2 wants the tester's dominant below 0.2*Vb: against the ECU's 510 ohm alone that is 12*33/543 = 0.73 V, and with the optional pull-up below also stuffed it is 1.38 V, both inside 2.4 V. Sized down from 100 ohm for exactly that second case. A sustained short of K-line to battery while transmitting puts 364 mA through the FET, over its 115 mA continuous rating -- it survives the pulse, not the fault. 1206 for the same reason

0-16V range: 16.0V in -> ~2.67V at the ADC (1k series included)

Lower leg: trips at 1.24V * 40.7/12.0 = 4.20V. The rail sits at 4.5-4.7V loaded (USB 5 V less the dev board's Schottky and the cable drop), and the LDO above holds 3.3 V down to about 3.6 V in, so 4.20 is inside the margin at both ends
Cathode pull-up. 10k gives the part 330uA, over the TLV431's 100uA minimum cathode current
Divide by 13.2, not 11: at 36V the 11:1 divider put 3.27V on the pin, above the ADC's usable 3.1V, so the reading saturated near the top of the declared input window
Hysteresis, about 0.1 V at the rail. A USB rail is noisier than a battery and the trip point is only 300 mV below the working level, so this matters more here than it did on the parent

Power-fail comparator. Below the trip point it stops conducting and R_pu takes PWR_FAIL high, so the interrupt is a rising edge and an absent or dead part reads as 'failing' rather than as 'fine'. PINOUT: this uses KiCad's TL431DBZ numbering (1 K, 2 REF, 3 A) on a plain SOT-23. Shunt references are NOT consistent between vendors in this package -- CONFIRM against the datasheet for the exact part ordered. If REF and A are swapped the part simply never conducts and PWR_FAIL sits permanently asserted: loud, harmless, and obvious on the bench, but it will not be caught by ERC or DRC
5 V buffer so WS2812 DIN is a real 5 V rail, not 3.3 V hoping
